card.name: The word plan and its verbs
card.fires_on: The word plan, plans or scheme as a subject, and the verb right after it (been, are, were, was). Mostly in narrative history or news about a planned operation.

modes.label: Plan as subject
modes.description: The noun plan, plans or scheme itself, starting a sentence or clause about what happened to it.
modes.example: The<< plan>> ended in disaster with eight of his group

modes.label: Verb after plan
modes.description: The auxiliary verb that follows plan or plans, before the outcome such as foiled, announced or approved.
modes.example: Without hesitation, the plan<< was>> approved by President Lincoln, General William Sheridan

card.writes: It promotes words like foiled, formulated and succeeded, and suppresses goal words, so it pushes toward what became of a plan.
card.plain: It lights up when a sentence is about a plan or scheme, and it expects to hear if the plan was foiled, announced or carried out.
